narrative: THE CEASEFIRE HOLDS - Dawn breaks over the Suwalki corridor for the first time in three days without the thunder of artillery. At precisely 06:00 CET, a 72-hour humanitarian ceasefire takes effect across all fronts. Russian forces withdraw the Western District from 50km to 100km from the Polish border. Belarusian forces pull back 20km from Lithuanian positions. NATO halts all air operations over Kaliningrad and the Baltic. In a converted warehouse outside Vilnius, International Red Cross convoys prepare to evacuate 7,000 trapped Lithuanian civilians. The first buses cross Belarusian lines at 08:30 under Turkish and German observation - mothers clutching children, elderly couples supporting each other, a teenager filming on his phone. By noon, 4,200 are through. The US F-16 pilot, Captain Jennifer Rodriguez, is released to Red Cross custody in Minsk at 14:00, walking across the tarmac to a US Air Force C-17. In Istanbul, delegations arrive for the Ankara Ceasefire Conference opening at 12:00 - US Secretary of State Rubio, Russian Foreign Minister Lavrov, German Foreign Minister Baerbock, Polish FM Sikorski, Turkish FM Fidan chairing. France de-escalates from tactical nuclear readiness to elevated posture, Macron declaring 'deterrence succeeded.' Oil drops from $125 to $105 on ceasefire news. EUR/USD recovers to $1.02 as German coalition stabilizes. The question now is whether the 72 hours leads to permanent settlement or merely postpones the inevitable. But for 7,000 Lithuanian families, and for the exhausted soldiers holding positions across the corridor, this dawn brings something neither side could achieve militarily: hope.
